summary: X-Forwarded-User header base64 encoding mismatch causes scheduled batch workers to receive 403 in private VPC
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports scheduled batch workers in their private VPC are intermittently receiving 403 Unauthorized when calling Redwood inference endpoints. Failures began after a recent on-prem edge proxy upgrade.

Impact:
- Multiple nightly batch jobs (DataScale internal ETL + model scoring) are failing to authenticate and retrying until SLA windows are missed.
- Affects only private deployment (customer_tier=private) in us-west region.
- Approx 18% of job runs failing since 2026-03-08 23:00 UTC.

Environment:
- Private control plane + VPC peering (us-west-2).
- On-prem edge proxy: AcmeEdge v3.4.1 (recently rolled on 2026-03-08).
- Scheduled workers: containerized batch workers authenticating via service-account impersonation; auth header passed by edge -> identity-proxy -> Redwood ingress.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a scheduled worker job that performs service-account token exchange and calls the Redwood private endpoint (/v1/infer).
2) Capture HTTP flow at edge and at customer-facing ingress.
3) Observe 403 responses from Redwood when the X-Forwarded-User header is present and appears to be base64-encoded.

Observed behavior:
- Edge proxy now emits X-Forwarded-User header encoded using URL-safe Base64 ("B64URL" where '+' -> '-', '/' -> '_', padding '=' may be stripped).
- Identity-proxy expects standard Base64 and attempts to decode; when it encounters URL-safe variants, decode fails silently and the request is treated as unauthenticated (role mapping fallback -> anonymous -> 403).
- Not all requests are affected (only clients/worker images that use the new edge upgrade configuration).

Expected behavior:
- Identity-proxy should robustly accept both standard Base64 and URL-safe Base64 for X-Forwarded-User and normalize to canonical representation before role lookups.

Relevant logs/headers (redacted):
- Example edge header captured: X-Forwarded-User: eyJ1c2VyIjoic2VydmljZS1hY2NvdW50In0t_ (note '-' and '_' present, padding dropped).
- Identity-proxy decode error seen in proxy debug logs at 2026-03-09T02:12:45Z: "failed to decode X-Forwarded-User: illegal base64 data at input byte 43"
- Ingress returned 403 with message: "anonymous access not allowed"

Workaround suggested to customer (temporary):
- Roll back edge proxy config to emit standard Base64 for X-Forwarded-User OR add a header transform rule at edge to pad/replace characters back before forwarding.
- Customer applied header-rewrite in AcmeEdge that replaced '-' -> '+' and '_' -> '/' then re-padded, reduced failure rate to ~1.5% (partial mitigation).

Notes:
- Related to header normalization behavior that was hardened in identity-proxy during previous security tightening change (see linked PR).
- Appears to be a compatibility regression after edge vendor changed default encoding for ergonomics.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Aisha Patel: Ticket opened after customer support case. Customer provided pcap and example headers; reporting degraded nightly job success rate. Asked for urgent triage.

2026-03-11 14:50 - Identity Team (Ravi Singh): Confirmed root cause. identity-proxy decoder uses strict StdEncoding from encoding/base64; will update to accept RawURLEncoding and fallback with padding. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1897

investigation_notes:
- Root cause: identity-proxy used strict standard base64 decoder; AcmeEdge started emitting URL-safe base64 without padding.
- Repro steps validated in staging.
- Hypothesis: silent decode failure causes request to bypass principal extraction, triggering default anonymous path.
- Confirmed with printer logs and end-to-end header captures.
- Risk assessment: low risk code change but affects auth path; must include thorough unit tests for decoder and golden vectors for padded/stripped variants.
- Rollout plan: canary in us-west-2 (10% traffic) -> monitor auth success rate and 403 counts for 24h -> full rollout.
resolution: IN PROGRESS - code fix merged to main after review. Hotfix built (identity-proxy v1.3.5-hotfix) and scheduled for canary deploy 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC. Post-deploy actions: monitor /metrics/auth_success_rate and 403 counts for 48h; reach out to DataScale to remove header-rewrite after successful canary. Follow-ups: add unit tests for URL-safe/standard/stripped padding variants, update identity-proxy runbook to mention header encoding compatibility, and notify partners about expected header formats in Private runbook.
